top_candidates.original_title: DMARC has been public since 2012 but most company domains still don't enforce it
top_candidates.generated_headline: Why DMARC Enforcement Fails: Misconfiguration, Ignored Policies, and the Identity Problem
top_candidates.summary: Email authentication protocols like DMARC suffer from practical friction and widespread misconfiguration. System administrators routinely ignore enforcement policies to avoid dropping legitimate email from misconfigured senders, while spammers easily pass authentication checks, leaving the fundamental problem of sender trust unsolved. Quote: The core problem is that the real need of email end users need is a way of determining whether or not to trust a given sender.
